https://www.hurriyetdailynews.com/turkiy.text: Türkiye to deploy F-16s to Estonia for NATO’s News Türkiye July 26 2026 14:57:56 Türkiye to deploy F-16s to Estonia for NATO’s The Turkish Air Force will once again contribute to NATO ’s Baltic Air Policing mission by deploying five F-16 fighter jets and 76 personnel from the 181st Jet Squadron Command, also known as Panther Squadron, to Amari Air Base in Estonia. The contingent, based at the 8th Main Jet Base Command in the southeastern province of Diyarbakır, will serve from August through November, maintaining round-the-clock quick reaction alert (QRA) duties to respond to potential airspace violations over the Baltic region. Speaking to Turkish state-run Anadolu Agency, before the deployment, a senior official from the command described air policing as a peacetime air defense mission carried out under NATO to safeguard allied airspace. He noted that the Baltic Air Policing mission is specifically designed to protect the airspace of Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania, which do not operate fighter aircraft of their own. During the deployment, Turkish crews will remain on continuous alert against unidentified aircraft or possible airspace incursions while also participating in joint activities with other NATO allies. First Lt. Özmen, one of the pilots assigned to the mission, said rigorous and continuous training is the key to maintaining the squadron’s high operational standards. He underlined that the success of every fighter sortie depends on the coordinated efforts of maintenance crews, air traffic controllers, planners and support personnel, emphasizing that teamwork is as important as pilot skill. NATO’s Baltic Air Policing mission is a standing peacetime operation that ensures the security of allied airspace through the permanent presence of fighter aircraft and crews on 24/7 quick reaction alert. It has been carried out since Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania joined the alliance in 2004. https://www.dailyecho.co.uk/news/2641372.text: Business Fareham Barnbrook Systems attends Farnborough Airshow for 16th year By William Dalgleish Reporter Share 0 Comments Andrew Barnett, managing director of Barnbrook Systems. (Image: Barnbrook Systems) This article is brought to you by our exclusive subscriber partnership with our sister title USA Today, and has been written by our American colleagues. It does not necessarily reflect the view of The Herald. A record-breaking year at the Farnborough International Airshow has put a spotlight on the growing importance of global defence and technology. Barnbrook Systems, headquartered in Fareham , marked its 16th consecutive appearance at the airshow by welcoming a record number of visitors from the UK and overseas. Andrew Barnett, managing director at Barnbrook Systems, said: "It was a record year at an airshow which had a very different feel about it. "There was a greater focus than ever on defence and especially upon the application of technology for the rapidly evolving nature of modern warfare. READ MORE: Market traders frustrated over being 'turfed out' during busiest months "It was also telling that many operators, primes and militaries were seeking improved efficiencies to extend the operational life and effectiveness of their platforms amid budgetary pressures despite increasing geo-political instability." The company showcased a range of technologies at its stand, including Maintenance, Repair and Overhaul (MRO) services, its BlueCube-powered sensing and monitoring technology, and the E:BAG lithium-ion battery fire suppression device developed in partnership with Flair. Mr Barnett, who is also a board member of the Farnborough Aerospace Consortium (FAC), said: "We are now following up on contacts made at the show and business opportunities around the world to support Barnbrook’s strategic growth and support the UK and allied defence infrastructure." Among the visitors to the Barnbrook stand were MPs and representatives from Germany, the US, France, India, and Czechoslovakia. The firm also hosted a reception for the South Central Regional Defence and Security Cluster (SCRDSC), which Mr Barnett chairs. More than 120 delegates attended the SCRDSC breakfast event, held at the FAC stand, to network and explore new partnership opportunities. READ MORE: Dozens of businesses join campaign to protect free-roaming animals Defence Secretary Wes Streeting confirmed at the show that the government's £298b Defence Investment Plan will go ahead, including a £15bn uplift over the next four years. Mr Barnett said: "The Defence Investment Plan is finally out, and with the new government team in place, we are now more hopeful within the defence sector. "Mr Streeting must be prepared to fight the corner of defence and secure even greater investment, which must make its way down the supply chain through prime contractors to SMEs."
